title: Sean O'Malley Admits One Childhood Decision He Wishes Someone Had Changed - NewsBreak
text:
By Sarthak Khanna ,
1 hours ago
Sean O’Malley (Image Credits: Imagn) Sean O’Malley has built a reputation as one of the most dynamic strikers in mixed martial arts. O’Malley is known for his flashy style, sharp movement, and knockout power inside the UFC octagon. However, the former bantamweight champion recently admitted that he sometimes looks back on his childhood and wishes someone had nudged him toward a different sport earlier.
Speaking candidly about his upbringing, O’Malley reflected on the sports he played as a child. He also shed light on how wrestling was never really part of the plan. Like many American kids, his after-school routine revolved around traditional team sports. “After school, we had football practice, basketball practice, baseball practice,” O’Malley said while recalling his younger years.
Looking back, O’Malley joked that he used to enjoy avoiding the grueling conditioning that wrestling typically involves. “I wish so much somebody was like, ‘Hey, maybe we should wrestle?’ I was like, ‘Heh, I’m playing basketball while you f*ckers running stairs and I’m shooting hoops.’”
While sports like football and basketball helped shape his athleticism, the 29-year-old admitted he now believes wrestling could have given him a valuable head start in combat sports. Wrestling is widely considered one of the most important foundations in MMA, with many elite fighters beginning their athletic careers on the mat long before transitioning to striking.
Sean O’Malley Reflects on How Wrestling Could Have Shaped His MMA Career Sean O’Malley (Image Credit: Getty Images) Despite the missed opportunity, O’Malley eventually found his way into combat sports and developed into one of the UFC’s most recognizable fighters. Known as “Sugar,” he carved out a career built largely on elite striking, creativity, and highlight-reel finishes.
However, wrestling has long been viewed as a key component for success in MMA, especially in the bantamweight division. Fighters with strong wrestling backgrounds often control the flow of the fight, giving them an advantage over strikers.
O’Malley has improved his grappling and defensive wrestling significantly over the years. He acknowledged that starting the discipline earlier might have made a difference in his development .
Even so, his career trajectory suggests that things worked out just fine. O’Malley rose through the ranks after gaining attention on Dana White’s Contender Series. He later captured the UFC bantamweight title, becoming one of the promotion’s biggest stars.
